title: Dry-fit and peg a mortise-and-tenon frame corner
instruction: Assemble the frame corner and peg it.
context: Furniture makers and joiners dry-fit every frame joint before glue-up: the tenon is lined up with its mortise and pushed home along the only direction it can move (1 mm clearance a side), then a peg is driven through stile and tenon to lock it. Order matters: the peg passes only once the tenon's hole is under the stile's, and a peg put in first blocks the mortise. Unlike peg-in-hole tasks, the robot has to seat one part against a shoulder before a second insertion becomes possible. Done by: cabinetmakers and bench carpenters (O*NET 51-7011.00).
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left); bench top is z 0. Stile: a 28 x 5 x 2 cm pine stile, clamped (fixed) flat on the bench, its long axis along y from y -14 to 14, its near edge at x 33. It has a through mortise 3.2 cm wide (y) x 1.0 cm tall, centred at y 0 and in the thickness, running through the full 5 cm width, and a 1.2 cm square peg hole bored vertically through the stile face at x 35.5, y 0, crossing the mortise. Rail: a loose 20 x 4 x 2 cm pine rail (73 g), lying flat with its long axis along x, its shoulder at x 27, y -13; its through tenon is 3.0 x 0.8 cm, 5.4 cm long, centred in the rail's thickness, its last 0.6 cm stepped in 2 mm a side, with a hole 1.3 cm along it and 1.2 cm across whose centre is 2.5 cm from the shoulder. Peg: a loose 1.0 x 1.0 x 5.0 cm square oak peg (3.5 g) standing upright in a fixed 4 x 4 x 1.5 cm grey block with a 1.2 cm square through hole, centred at x 30, y 10.
scoring: From the parts' poses at the end (a tape measure and a photo on a real rig). Tenon home: the rail's shoulder within 2 mm of the stile's near edge and the rail's centre line within 3 mm of the mortise's. Pegged: the peg's lowest point within 4 mm of the bench (through the tenon; a peg resting on a tenon whose hole is not lined up stands 14 mm up), its centre within 4 mm of the hole's axis, tilted under 10 deg, let go (grippers 2.5 cm clear) and still. The rail must be let go and still for any credit. 1.0 tenon home and pegged, success when held 1 s; 0.5 tenon home, not pegged; 0.2 tenon at least 2.5 cm into the mortise but not home; else 0. Scored at the last step. Possible scores: 0, 0.2, 0.5, 1.0.
reset_notes: Pull the peg and the rail out, stand the peg in its block and lay the rail on its marks; the stile stays clamped.
fidelity: Rigid boxes, one shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic); wood is not compressible, so the tenon is a sliding fit (1 mm a side) rather than a tight one and the peg a 1 mm-clearance fit rather than a drawbored interference fit. The mortise, holes and chamfer are built from boxes; the peg is square, not riven or round. The stile is fixed in place, standing in for bench clamps.
